what_it_is.prose: Project-75(I) is the Indian Navy's programme to procure six conventional diesel-electric submarines equipped with Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) technology, under the Strategic Partnership model of the Defence Procurement Procedure. The programme is valued at approximately ₹40,000 crore and represents the largest single Make-in-India defence contract. The bid is pending between two consortia: (1) Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) partnered with ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems of Germany, offering a variant of the Type 214 submarine; and (2) Larsen & Toubro (L&T) partnered with Navantia of Spain, offering the S80 Plus submarine. The critical evaluation criterion is AIP technology transfer — both bidders have operational AIP systems (Navantia's is on the Spanish Navy's S81 Isaac Peral; ThyssenKrupp's is on multiple export customers' Type 214s). The predecessor Project-75 delivered six Scorpene-class submarines (INS Kalvari to INS Vagsheer) built by MDL with Naval Group of France, with the last (INS Vagsheer) commissioned in 2025. The Indian Navy's submarine fleet is aging and the P-75(I) is critical to maintaining underwater capability. Separately, L&T is leading India's Project-76 indigenous diesel-electric submarine design effort, with a target design completion by 2027.

deployments_procurement.summary: Project-75(I) is in the bid evaluation phase as of August 2026. The two competing consortia are MDL+ThyssenKrupp (Germany) and L&T+Navantia (Spain), with the final MoD decision pending. The programme value is approximately ₹40,000 crore for 6 AIP-equipped submarines. No production contract has been signed.

faq.question: Who are the two bidders for Project-75(I)?
faq.answer: Two consortia submitted bids for the ₹40,000 crore Project-75(I) programme: (1) Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited (MDL) partnered with ThyssenKrupp Marine Systems of Germany, offering a variant of the Type 214 submarine; and (2) Larsen & Toubro (L&T) partnered with Navantia of Spain, offering the S80 Plus submarine. Both bidders have operational Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) systems, which is the critical evaluation criterion. The final MoD decision was pending as of August 2026.

faq.question: Why is AIP technology critical for Project-75(I)?
faq.answer: Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) allows a conventional diesel-electric submarine to operate submerged for extended periods without surfacing or snorkelling — typically 2-3 weeks vs a few days for non-AIP boats. This dramatically reduces the submarine's detectability and is considered essential for the Indian Navy's operational requirements in the Indian Ocean Region. Both ThyssenKrupp (Germany) and Navantia (Spain) have operational AIP systems, with Navantia's on the Spanish Navy's S81 Isaac Peral.

faq.question: What is the relationship between Project-75(I) and Project-76?
faq.answer: Project-75(I) is the near-term programme to procure 6 AIP-equipped conventional submarines from a foreign OEM with Indian Strategic Partner under ToT. Project-76 is a separate, longer-term programme led by L&T to design an indigenous diesel-electric submarine, with a target design completion by 2027. Project-76 represents India's path to sovereign submarine design capability, while Project-75(I) addresses immediate capability gaps.
